match.userMessage: Storyboard animatic frame. wide. eye level. Handheld observational view of the bakery entrance and street; MARA is framed by the doorway, with the opposite side of the road visible. MARA stands at the bakery entrance beside the shop sign, ready to turn it; CYCLIST is not yet in frame. Then: MARA flips the sign to OPEN and steps into the morning light as CYCLIST waves from across the road. Camera: handheld follow, natural, lightly responsive. Hold the street's distance between them as the greeting carries across. Characters: MARA: Female, 30s, A woman in her 30s, of average height and sturdy, capable build. She has dark brown hair tied back in a practical bun, brown eyes, and a lightly flour-marked face. No permanent marks are specified, wearing A white cotton baker’s shirt, a flour-dusted natural-canvas apron, dark work trousers, and sturdy black nonslip shoes. CYCLIST: Unspecified, 20s–40s, A delivery cyclist seen across the road, of average height and lean build. Their features are not described; for visual continuity, they have short dark hair and a neutral, friendly expression. No permanent marks are specified, wearing A practical dark cycling jacket, fitted trousers, and a bicycle helmet; a compact delivery bag is worn on the back. Drawn as a storyboard artist's animatic frame: confident pencil line with flat grey marker tones, three or four values, greyscale only even where the description names a colour. Clear silhouettes, correct perspective and depth, the set blocked in with simple shapes. Figures have readable poses, gestures and simple expressive faces. Draw the single opening moment of the shot: each character appears exactly once, and what happens next is shown only by a few bold arrows for the camera move and the way subjects travel. A rough pre-production drawing: not a finished illustration, not a photo, not a 3D render. The drawing fills the whole image edge to edge: no border, no frame line, no paper margin, no grid of panels.
